chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: His godmother Jesse Knight
summary: Collins lived with his godmother, a fair-skinned Montgomery pianist who worked as a governess and joined the post office in her sixties.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You said -- you mentioned at one point that you were living with your God mother whom you said was a very good musician.

Her name was Jesse Knight. She was from Montgomery, she was a very fair woman, very -- the red hair, long red hair, and her father was -- reminded me of Santa Claus. He had a flowing white beard, and he was -- well, he was white, you know, really. And when I went to New York I told you I stayed at the Woodside, was my first place to stay. And I got tired of that and I went to live with her.
Did she work professionally for you?
No, she didn't play. She was --
Oh, that's right, you didn't say she was a

She played very fine piano. But she was like a very -- she was an unusual woman. She was a highly intelligent woman, and she was governess for say like the big, rich families. I mean, a governess. Dietician, you know. And when she was in her late sixties she decided that she wanted to work at the post office, and she took the exams and they never knew -- she was such an agile woman, and such fine physical condition they never knew how old she was. So she worked there until she got out. I think she worked there for years, for six, seven years there. Until she got tired and she quit. This is the type of woman she was. [PAUSE]
